+# Schema-Driven Type Safety for Database Queries
+
+## Problem
+Production incidents from schema changes (e.g., renamed columns) weren't caught until running against real data, because TypeScript treated SQL strings as unchecked strings.
+
+## Solution: Kysely + Auto-Generated Schema Types
+
+### How it works
+
+1. **Type Generation (Build Time)**
+   ```bash
+   npm run type-gen
+   ```
+   This runs `kysely-codegen` which introspects your Postgres database and generates `src/db/types.ts` with full TypeScript interfaces for every table. This becomes the source of truth.
+
+2. **Type-Safe Queries**
+   Queries use Kysely's type-safe API instead of raw SQL strings:
+   ```typescript
+   // Before: Not type-checked
+   const result = await pool.query("SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users WHERE id = $1", [id]);
+
+   // After: Full type safety
+   const user = await db
+     .selectFrom("users")
+     .select(["id", "email", "created_at"])
+     .where("id", "=", id)
+     .executeTakeFirst();
+   ```
+
+3. **Catch Schema Changes at Compile Time**
+   If a migration renames `created_at` → `created_timestamp`:
+   - `npm run type-gen` regenerates types
+   - TypeScript immediately flags the error: `Property 'created_at' does not exist on Users`
+   - Build fails; code never reaches production ✓
+
+### How to use this setup
+
+#### First time (or when adding new tables)
+```bash
+# Set DATABASE_URL to your Postgres database
+export DATABASE_URL="postgres://user:pass@localhost/dbname"
+
+# Generate types from the current schema
+npm run type-gen
+
+# Check that src/db/types.ts was created with your table definitions
+```
+
+#### After migrations
+```bash
+# After deploying a migration (column rename, new table, etc.)
+npm run type-gen
+
+# TypeScript will flag any query that references old columns
+npm run build
+
+# If queries fail type-check, fix them before merging
+```
+
+#### Adding a new query
+```typescript
+// New queries automatically get type-checking
+export const findActiveUsers = async () => {
+  return await db
+    .selectFrom("users")
+    .select(["id", "email"]) // ← TypeScript error if "email" doesn't exist
+    .where("status", "=", "active")
+    .execute();
+};
+```
+
+### Build integration
+
+Add to your CI/CD pipeline:
+```bash
+npm run type-gen  # Regenerate types from current schema
+npm run build     # Build and type-check all queries
+```
+
+This ensures every deployed query matches the current schema.
+
+### Why Kysely?
+
+- **Auto-generates types from live schema** — No separate schema file to maintain
+- **SQL-like API** — Familiar to the hand-written SQL style, minimal learning curve
+- **Catches schema drift at compile time** — Not at runtime
+- **Lightweight** — Thin wrapper over pg, not an ORM overhead
+- **No manual type annotations** — Codegen keeps types in sync automatically
+
+### Trade-offs
+
+| Aspect | Raw pg | Kysely |
+|--------|--------|--------|
+| Type safety | None | Complete |
+| Learning curve | None | Low |
+| Runtime overhead | Minimal | Negligible |
+| Schema sync | Manual | Automatic |
+| Production incidents from schema drift | Yes | No |
+
+### When the database isn't available at build time
+
+If you can't introspect the database during CI (e.g., no staging DB access), you can:
+1. Generate types locally and commit `src/db/types.ts` to git
+2. In CI, skip type generation and use committed types
+3. After migrations deploy, regenerate types locally and commit the update
+
+This keeps types synchronized with deployed schema while allowing CI-only builds.

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/kysely.config.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+import type { GenerateConfig } from "kysely-codegen";
+
+const config: GenerateConfig = {
+  dialect: "postgres",
+  connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
+  outFile: "src/db/types.ts",
+};
+
+export default config;

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+import type { ColumnType } from "kysely";
+
+export type Generated<T> = T extends ColumnType<infer S, any, any> ? ColumnType<S, S | undefined, S> : ColumnType<T, T | undefined, T>;
+export type Timestamp = ColumnType<Date, Date | string, Date | string>;
+
+export interface AuditLog {
+  id: Generated<number>;
+  actor: string;
+  action: string;
+  created_at: Generated<Timestamp>;
+}
+
+export interface Users {
+  id: string;
+  email: string;
+  created_at: Timestamp;
+}
+
+export interface DB {
+  audit_log: AuditLog;
+  users: Users;
+}
